labs.title: Build an approval cloud flow in Power Automate
labs.summary: Create an automated cloud flow triggered by a Dataverse row, add a first-responder approval, branch on the outcome, update status, send email, and test the run.
labs.scenario: Contoso Facilities wants every new equipment request to start an approval automatically. In the **simulated Power Automate** portal, create an **Automated cloud flow** that runs when an **Equipment Request** row is added in Dataverse, starts and waits for a first-responder approval, updates the request status to **Approved** or **Rejected**, emails the requester, and passes Flow checker before a manual test run. Everything is simulated; no real email or approval is sent.
learningObjectives: Choose an event-driven automated cloud flow for a Dataverse row creation scenario
Configure a Dataverse trigger, an approval action and a condition in the flow designer
Explain how triggers, actions, connectors, cloud flows and desktop flows differ
prerequisites: Know that a trigger starts a cloud flow and actions run after the trigger

steps.title: Create an automated cloud flow
steps.instruction: Select **Create**, choose **Automated cloud flow**, name it **Equipment request approval**, choose **When a row is added, modified or deleted - Microsoft Dataverse**, and select **Create**.
steps.hint: Do not choose Instant or Scheduled. This process starts from a Dataverse event.
steps.explanation: Automated cloud flows are event-driven. Instant flows start from a manual action; scheduled flows start from a clock.

rules.description: An automated Dataverse-triggered cloud flow exists
rules.failureFeedback: Create an Automated cloud flow, not an instant or scheduled flow.

steps.title: Configure the Dataverse trigger
steps.instruction: On the trigger card, set **Change type** to **Added**, **Table name** to **Equipment Requests**, and **Scope** to **Organization**, then select **Apply**.
steps.hint: Organization scope watches rows created by anyone in the environment.
steps.explanation: A trigger defines what event starts the flow. The Dataverse connector listens for rows in a selected table and scope.

rules.description: Trigger uses Added, Equipment Requests and Organization
rules.failureFeedback: Set Change type Added, Table name Equipment Requests, and Scope Organization.

steps.title: Add a first-responder approval
steps.instruction: Select **+ Add an action**, add **Start and wait for an approval**, set **Approval type** to **Approve/Reject - First to respond**, **Assigned to** to **manager@contoso.example**, and include requester, quantity, and request date dynamic content in **Details**.
steps.hint: Everyone must approve is for scenarios where every listed approver must respond.
steps.explanation: The Approvals connector creates an approval request and waits until the required response condition is met.

rules.description: Approval action is first responder and assigned to the manager
rules.failureFeedback: Add Start and wait for an approval with Approve/Reject - First to respond.

steps.title: Branch on the approval outcome
steps.instruction: Select **Add a condition**. Configure **Outcome is equal to Approve**. In **If yes**, add **Update a row** with Status **Approved** and **Send an email (V2)** to the requester. In **If no**, add **Update a row** with Status **Rejected** and **Send an email (V2)** to the requester.
steps.hint: Both branches need a Dataverse update and an Outlook email action.
steps.explanation: Conditions split a flow into branches so the automation can do different work for approved and rejected outcomes.

rules.description: Condition branches update status and email the requester
rules.failureFeedback: Configure Outcome equals Approve, then update Approved/Rejected status and email the requester in both branches.

steps.title: Save, check and test the flow
steps.instruction: Select **Save**, then **Flow checker** and confirm there are no errors. Select **Test** and run the manual test so the run history shows **Succeeded** with approval response **Approve**.
steps.hint: The test simulates creating a Dataverse row and approving the request.
steps.explanation: Flow checker catches configuration errors before a run. Run history confirms whether each trigger and action succeeded.

rules.failureFeedback: Run Flow checker after all required cards are configured.
Use Test after saving and checking the flow; the run history should show Succeeded.

labs.solution:
1. Select **Create** > **Automated cloud flow**.
2. Enter flow name `Equipment request approval`, choose **When a row is added, modified or deleted - Microsoft Dataverse**, and select **Create**.
3. On the trigger, set **Change type** to **Added**, **Table name** to **Equipment Requests**, and **Scope** to **Organization**. Select **Apply**.
4. Select **+ Add an action**, add **Start and wait for an approval**, set **Approval type** to **Approve/Reject - First to respond**, **Assigned to** to `manager@contoso.example`, and use dynamic content in **Details** for requester, quantity, and request date.
5. Select **Add a condition** and configure **Outcome is equal to Approve**.
6. In **If yes**, add **Update a row** setting Status to `Approved`, then **Send an email (V2)** to the requester. In **If no**, add **Update a row** setting Status to `Rejected`, then **Send an email (V2)** to the requester.
7. Select **Save**, run **Flow checker** until it shows no errors, then select **Test** > **Manually** and complete the simulated approval response. Confirm run history shows **Succeeded**.
